en: The Great King of Teachings for the Direct Realization of the Mahāyāna, Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas, Vajraśekhara Sūtra, Volume One.
By [the monk] who held the rank of Kaifu Yitongsisi, Teci, and Acting Minister of State Ceremonies during the Sui Dynasty.

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works, bearing the posthumous title Dajian (Great Mirror), the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, translated by imperial decree: *The Chapter on the Extensive Ritual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu*, Part One. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Bhagavat attained the supreme samaya-wisdom of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas;
he received the consecration of the Dharma King of the Three Realms from the jeweled crowns of all Tathāgatas, and realized all...
Having attained mastery in the yoga of omniscient wisdom (*sarvajñajñāna*), he is able to perform all the various activities of the seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas with equanimity;
he brings to complete fulfillment all the intentions and actions of the entire realm of sentient beings, without exception or end,
and as Mahāvairocana of Great Compassion, he dwells eternally throughout the three times.
The Tathāgata Vajra of all Body, Speech, and Mind dwells in the sporting realm of all Tathāgatas,
within the Great Maṇi Palace in the celestial palace of the King of Akaniṣṭha,
where various bells and silk banners are interspersed and stirred by a gentle breeze, and which is adorned with pearl garlands, necklaces, and crescent and full-moon ornaments.
The Bodhisattva Śrīvyūha was accompanied by a multitude of ninety koṭis of bodhisattvas—namely:

the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sadyaścittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganagañja, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvamārabalapramardin; these and others were the leaders of the assembly.
He manifests as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River—like sesame seeds filling Jambudvīpa—and likewise fills the Akaniṣṭha Heaven in the same manner.

From each and every one of those immeasurable bodies of the Tathāgatas, there appear immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields, and within those Buddha-fields, they in turn proclaim this very principle of the Dharma.

At that time, the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata—who eternally abides in all space; who is the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas; who is the mutual interpenetration of all Tathāgatas; who is the wisdom-sattva awakened to the entire Vajradhātu; who is the treasury of wisdom born from the vajra-consecration of the atoms of all space-realms;

who is infinite because he is all Tathāgatas; who is the great jewel of the consecration of great vajra-wisdom; who is the Tathatā-wisdom pervading all space; and who manifests the realization of *samyak-saṃbodhi* because the nature of his own self is pure as all Tathāgatas—[spoke thus].

The self-nature purity of all phenomena, pervading all of space, the wisdom capable of manifesting all forms without exception, the supreme conduct for taming the realm of sentient beings because it issues the non-empty commands of all Tathāgatas;
the supreme skillful wisdom that is entirely equal, the firm *sattva* of the great bodhi of all Tathāgatas, the samaya of summoning of all Tathāgatas,
and the mastery of wisdom in accordance with the defilements of all Tathāgatas.
The "Excellent! of all Tathāgatas; the jewel of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas;
the circular radiance of the solar disc of all Tathāgatas; the cintāmaṇi-jewel banner of the king of contemplation of all Tathāgatas;
the great laughter of all Tathāgatas; the great, pure Dharma of all Tathāgatas; and the prajñā-wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
The wheel of all Tathāgatas; the secret speech of all Tathāgatas;
the various non-empty activities of all Tathāgatas; the wondrous, firm, and solid armor of the great diligence of all Tathāgatas;
the Vajra Yakṣa who universally protects all Tathāgatas; the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Seal-Wisdom. Samantabhadra,
Sublime Amoghasiddhi, Mārajit, Lord of Great Joy, Gaganagañja,
Great Sublime Light, Ratnaketu, and Great Smile.
One is able to contemplate Maheśvara, Mañjuśrī, and all the maṇḍalas;
the various activities are beyond words, characterized by diligence, wrath, and firm resolve.
There is the Vajra Hook, Arrow, and Joy; the Jewel, Sun, Banner, and Laughter.
The Lotus, Sword, and Wondrous Wheel; holding the Karmic Armor and the Terrible.
Beginningless and endless quiescence; Fierce Anger and Great Patience.
Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the Valiant; the Majestic and the Greatly Wealthy.
The Lord of the World, the Vaishravana; Vishnu, the Victorious One, the Great Peaceful One;
the World-Protectors, Space, and Earth; the Three Times and the Three Realms;
the Great Elements that benefit virtuous people; and all the Pitṛs and Grandfathers.
The constant flow and nirvāṇa, the Great Awakening within the true flow;
the pure Mahāyāna awakening, the eternal one among the three realms of existence;
Trailokyavijaya who partakes in bliss, the sovereign of all those who can subdue.
Firm Lord, Supreme Exalted Ground, Wisdom, the Ultimate Principle of the Other Shore,
Liberator, Awakener of Sentient Beings, One who Acts as All Tathāgatas.
Awakened Benefit, Buddha-Mind, The Unsurpassed State of All Bodhi.
The Sovereign King of Universal Illumination, Spontaneously possessing the dhāraṇī of mindfulness;
The Great Seal of the Great Sattva, The meditative absorption (*samādhi*) that performs the Buddha’s activities;
With all Buddhas as one's body, The Sattva constantly benefits awakening.
The Great Root, the Great Black One; the Great Passion, the Great Bliss;
the Great Expedient Means, the Great Victorious One; the Sovereign of all Victorious Palaces.
When the Bhagavat Mahābodhicitta Samantabhadra Mahābodhisattva dwells within the hearts of all Tathāgatas, all Tathāgatas fill this Buddha-world like sesame seeds.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas gathered like clouds and, approaching the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi as he sat at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), manifested their enjoyment bodies (*saṃbhogakāya*) and spoke thus:
"O son of noble family!..."
"How can one realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment while remaining ignorant of the true patience regarding all the ascetic practices of the Tathāgatas?
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, having been exhorted by all the Tathāgatas, arose from the *asaṃpramoṣaka* samādhi, prostrated before all the Tathāgatas, and addressed them, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgatas, you have instructed me:"
"How should one practice? What is the truth?
Having spoken thus, all the Tathāgatas, with one voice and in unison, addressed that Bodhisattva, saying:
“O son of noble family!
You should abide in the samādhi of observing oneself and recite at will with the mantra of self-nature accomplishment:
‘Oṃ citraprati-vi-taṅ-kāru-mi. At that time, the Bodhisattva addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:
“O World-Honored Tathāgata!
Having attained universal knowledge, I see my own mind in the form of a lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas replied:
“Good son! The self-nature of the mind is luminous, just as when one cultivates effort universally, one obtains results according to what is performed;
it is also like dyeing a white garment, which takes on color according to the dye applied.”
Then, in order to cause the wisdom-mind (*cittajñāna*) of natural luminosity to flourish, all the Tathāgatas further commanded those Bodhisattvas, saying:
"Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. By means of this mantra of essential accomplishment, they caused them to generate the bodhicitta.
Then that Bodhisattva, having further received the instructions from all the Tathāgatas and generated the bodhicitta, spoke these words:
"Just as that lunar disc is in form, I too am seen in the form of a lunar disc."
All the Tathāgatas replied:
"Since you have already generated the Samantabhadra mind of all the Tathāgatas, you have obtained the equalizing vajra.
Firmly and well-established in this generation of the Samantabhadra mind of all the Tathāgatas, contemplate the form of a vajra within the moon-disk of your own heart, using this mantra:"
"Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra. The Bodhisattva addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored Tathāgata!
I see a vajra within the lunar disc."
All the Tathāgatas spoke in unison:
“To make firm the Vajra of Samantabhadra’s Mind of all Tathāgatas, by means of this mantra:

‘Oṃ vajratma jhaṃ. All the vajra realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, which pervade the entirety of the realm of empty space, are empowered by all the Tathāgatas and enter entirely into the Sattvavajra. Thus, all the Tathāgatas confer upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi the consecration of the Vajradhātu with the vajra-name ‘Vajradhātu.’”
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhātu addressed all those Tathāgatas, saying:
“World-Honored Tathāgatas!
I perceive all Tathāgatas as my own self.”
All the Tathāgatas spoke again: "Therefore, Mahāsattva!
Having accomplished all forms through the Vajra of All Beings, visualize yourself in the form of a Buddha and recite this mantra of natural accomplishment as you wish:”

Having uttered these words—“Oṃ yathā sarvatathāgata-satya-haṃ”—the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhātu manifested his own body as the Tathāgata. After prostrating to all the Tathāgatas, he addressed them, saying:
“I pray that the World-Honored Ones, all the Tathāgatas, empower me so that this realization of awakening may become firm.”
Having spoken these words, all the Tathāgatas entered into the Vajradhātu Tathāgata within that Sattvavajra.

At that very moment, the Blessed One Vajradhātu Tathāgata realized the equalizing wisdom of all the Tathāgatas; he entered the samaya of the equalizing wisdom of all the Tathāgatas, and having realized the self-nature purity of the equalizing wisdom of the Dharma of all the Tathāgatas, he became the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sarvatathāgatasamatāsvabhāvaprabhāsvarajñānagarbha.

Then all the Tathāgatas again emerged from the Sattvavajra of all the Tathāgatas; they conferred the empowerment of the Great Maṇi Jewel of Ākāśagarbha, gave rise to the Dharma-wisdom of Avalokiteśvara, and established the Vaiśravaṇa-karma of all the Tathāgatas, whereby they proceeded to the summit of Mount Sumeru, to the pavilion of the Vajramaṇi-jewel peak.
Having arrived, Vajradhātu Tathāgata, empowered by all Tathāgatas, was established upon every side of the lion-thrones of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, Avalokiteśvararāja Tathāgata, Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata... and all the Tathāgatas empowered themselves with the empowerment of all Tathāgatas.
Because the Bhagavān Tathāgata Śākyamuni has attained perfect and equal mastery over all things, he sat observing the four directions with equanimity toward all quarters.

At that time, before long, the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata, manifested and proclaimed the universal awakening of the heart of Samantabhadra of all Tathāgatas; the attainment of the empowerment of the great maṇi-jewel arising from the space of all Tathāgatas; the reaching of the further shore of the dharma-knowledge of Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas; and the non-empty, unobstructed teaching of Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas, which perfects all activities and fulfills all aspirations.

The nature of all Tathāgatas confers empowerment upon one’s own body; thus, one enters the samaya of the Samantabhadra Mahābodhisattva of all Tathāgatas and gives rise to the Sattvādhiṣṭhānavajrasamādhi, the Great Vehicle realization-samaya of all Tathāgatas, known as the Heart of All Tathāgatas, which emerges from one’s own heart.

"Vajrasattva"—as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Bhagavat Samantabhadra became many moon discs, which universally purify the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings, and he remained surrounding all the Buddhas.
From those many moon discs, the wisdom-vajra of all Tathāgatas emerged and entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, by virtue of the firmness of Samantabhadra.

From the *vajrasattva-samādhi*, through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, they merge into a single entity; its magnitude exhausting the entirety of space, it becomes pervasive as light forming five peaks.
The vajra-forms born from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas and rested within the palms of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, from those vajras, vajra-forms of various colors and appearances emerged, extending and pervading to illuminate all worlds.
From that vajra-light gate, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerge,

pervading the entire Dharma-realm and reaching the furthest reaches of all space; they fill the ocean-like clouds of all worlds and universally realize the supernatural powers of the equal wisdom of all Tathāgatas, giving rise to the great bodhi of all Tathāgatas.
With the mind, one accomplishes the various practices of Samantabhadra, serves all Tathāgatas,
proceeds to the site of great enlightenment to subdue the armies of Māra, realizes the equal great enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, turns the wheel of the true Dharma,
and even rescues and benefits all beings without exception, bringing them peace and happiness throughout the entirety of existence.
In the realm of passion (*rāgadhātu*), having accomplished the supreme siddhi of the miraculous powers of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas and so forth,
and because he manifests the playful supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas as Samantabhadra and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is wondrously firm,
they gather into a single body, giving rise to the form of the Mahābodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! I, Samantabhadra, Am the natural, firm sattva;
From the firm and bodiless, I have attained the body of a sattva."
Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, stood before all the Tathāgatas upon a lunar disc, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the Bhagavān entered the Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, known as the Vajra-samādhi; it is the Samaya of Great Wisdom, the Power of Great Skillful Means, and Diligence, which partakes in the ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas, turns the wheel of the True Dharma, and benefits sentient beings. It exhausts and leaves no remainder in the realm of sentient beings, acting as their sovereign to bring them peace, happiness, and joy, until they attain the equalizing wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the supernatural powers, the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, and the direct realization of the fruit of the most supreme siddhi.

All the Tathāgatas, having conferred the Vajra of Accomplishment upon that Mahābodhisattva Samantabhadra and bestowed upon him the consecration of the Universal Monarch of All Tathāgatas, consecrated him with the jeweled crowns and silken ribbons of the bodies of all Buddhas, and then placed [the vajra] into his two hands.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajrapāṇi—conferred the Vajrapāṇi empowerment. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, with his left hand in the *māna* (haughty) gesture and his right hand dancing, brandished the *vajra*.
Placing that *vajra* at his own heart and assuming a posture of increasing power, he uttered this udāna: “This is the supreme vajra of all Buddhas;
It has been bestowed into the palm of my hand. The vajra is empowered by the vajra.”

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, the vajra-samādhi named "Sattvādhiṣṭhāna" produced therefrom, also known as the "Samaya for Summoning All Tathāgatas. From his own heart, the hearts of all Tathāgatas issued forth.
As soon as "Vajrarāja" emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became the great hook of all the Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, they entered the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana and condensed into a single entity, manifesting as the form of a great vajra hook (*vajrāṅkuśa*) and abiding within the Buddha’s palm.

From the form of the great vajra hook, there appeared bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, in order to summon all Tathāgatas and perform the wondrous and non-empty sovereign play of supernatural powers of all Buddhas; and because the *Vajrasattva-samādhi* is extremely firm, they condensed into a single entity, manifesting as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, who abided in the heart of Vairocana Buddha and uttered this udāna:
“O wonder! The Sovereign Amogha, The hook born of the Vajra!”
"By means of pervading all Buddhas, one accomplishes the hook-summoning.
At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja descended from the heart of the Buddha, took his place upon the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, and again requested instructions.

Then the Bhagavān entered the samādhi called the Vajra Samādhi of the Samaya of Hook-Summoning of All Tathāgatas; he received the samaya of the hook-summoning of all Tathāgatas and performed the summoning of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of bestowing all peace and joy, and even for the sake of the supreme siddhi of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas. Thereupon, he bestowed that Vajra Hook upon the hands of the Great Bodhisattva King Amoghasiddhi.

When all the Tathāgatas conferred the vajra-name—Vajrākarṣaṇa (Vajra Summoner)—during the Vajrākarṣaṇa empowerment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrākarṣaṇa summoned all the Tathāgatas with the Vajra Hook and uttered this udāna:
“This is the supreme vajra-wisdom of all Buddhas;
It accomplishes the benefit of all Buddhas, And is the most excellent means for summoning.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Māra, giving rise to the empowerment of the Sattva named the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya of Universal Adherence of All Tathāgatas, which is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas; it issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajrarāga" issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the flower weapon of all the Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, it enters the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and condenses into a single entity, manifesting as the form of a great vajra-arrow, which abides within the Buddha’s palm.

From that vajra-arrow form, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, performing the "staining" (*anurāga*) of all Tathāgatas and manifesting the supreme slaying through the miraculous play (*vikrīḍita*) of all Buddhas. Because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is utterly firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Māra. Abiding within the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! Self-nature is pure; Spontaneously stained by desire, yet purified by the absence of desire, It subdues beings through the very act of staining."
Then the body of that Great Bodhisattva Māra descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, rested upon the moon disc to the left of all Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the vajra-samādhi called "The Empowerment of Adherence to All Tathāgatas," and received the samaya of the "Slaying Power of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of bringing all realms of sentient beings, without exception, to every form of peace and joy, and until they attain the supreme siddhi-fruit of the *māra*-activity of all Tathāgatas, he then bestowed that vajra-arrow into the two hands of the Great Bodhisattva Māra.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra-name—Vajracāpa (Vajra-Bow)—at the time of the Vajracāpa empowerment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracāpa slew [the obstacles] with the vajra-arrow. All the Tathāgatas then spoke this udāna:
“This is the state of all Buddhas, A defiled wisdom free from blemish.
Through defilement, one harms and overcomes aversion, And is able to bestow all peace and happiness.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāpramuditārāja; from his own heart issued forth the vajra-samādhi called the "Sattvādhiṣṭhāna" (Empowerment of the Being), which is the "Supreme Joy Samaya of All Tathāgatas," known as the Heart of All Tathāgatas.

As soon as "Vajrasādhu" issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara manifested the gesture of "Excellent! (sādhu) for all the Tathāgatas; he entered the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, merged into a single entity, assumed the form of Great Joy, and remained within the Buddha’s palm.

From that form of Joy, there emerged Tathāgata bodies as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, manifesting the "Excellent" (*sādhu*) gesture of all Tathāgatas. Because they sported with the supernatural powers of all Buddhas in supreme joy, and because the *Vajrasattva-samādhi* was extremely firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāpramuditārāja.
Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna: "How marvelous! How excellent am I!
All those of supreme wisdom, Who are free from conceptual construction, Are able to give rise to ultimate joy."
Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Rāgarāja descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place upon the lunar disc behind all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instructions.

Then the World-Honored One entered the vajra-samādhi named "Empowerment of the Equal Joy of All Tathāgatas. Because he had received the equal joy, all peace, and all delight of all Tathāgatas; because he had attained the peerless joy, all peace, and all delight of all Tathāgatas; and because he had attained the supreme siddhi-fruit of the flavor of the unsurpassed joy of all Tathāgatas, he then placed that Vajra-Joy into the two hands of the Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pramuditarāja.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajrarati—when conferring the Vajrarati initiation, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrarati, with the gesture of "Excellent! (sādhu) of Vajrarati, gladdened all the Tathāgatas and uttered this udāna:
"This is the state of all Buddhas, Which can turn the gesture of 'Excellent!
Acting as the Vajra of All Joys, It causes sublime joy to increase."
The Great Bodhicitta, the Samaya for summoning all Tathāgatas, the Great Joy of the Wisdom of Universal Adherence of all Tathāgatas—such is the Mahāsattva of the Great Samaya of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, the vajra-samādhi named Jewel Empowerment, which is the samaya of the consecration of all Tathāgatas; it is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas and issued forth from his own heart.

Upon the mere emergence of "Vajraratna" from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, because of the thorough realization of the wisdom of equality throughout all space and because of the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they condensed into a single body.

Then that Bhagavān Vajradhara, having emerged as the Light of All Space, illuminated the entire realm of sentient beings with the light of all space, thereby forming the realm of all space; and through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, he entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Buddha Vairocana.

Through thorough cultivation, the samādhi of Vajrasattva—which is formed from the womb-matrix of the entire realm of space—manifests as a great adamantine jewel-form equal in extent to all pervading worlds, abiding within the palms of the Buddhas.

From that vajra-jewel form, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerge; having emerged, they perform the consecrations and other rites for all Tathāgatas, and manifest the miraculous play of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds.

Because it is the wondrous birth from the matrix of the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*), and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is extremely firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the form of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous is the sublime empowerment, The unsurpassed vajra-jewel.
Through the Buddha’s non-attachment, He is named the Lord of the Three Realms.”
Then the body of that Great Bodhisattva Gaganagañja descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, rested upon a moon disc before all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instructions.

Then the World-Honored One entered the Great Maṇi-jewel of all Tathāgatas, named the Vajra Samādhi, and received the samaya of the perfectly fulfilled aspirations of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of securing all benefits for the realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of receiving all peace, happiness, and joy, and even for the sake of attaining the supreme, glorious siddhi that benefits all Tathāgatas, he took that vajra-maṇi and conferred upon the Mahāsattva Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, the Vajra-Ratna-Cakravartin, the consecration of the vajra-ratna form, placing it in his two hands.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajragarbha—conferred the Vajragarbha empowerment. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha placed a vajra-maṇi upon his own place of empowerment and uttered this udāna:
“This is the empowerment of all Buddhas for the realm of sentient beings;
They have bestowed it into the palm of my hand, A jewel placed within a jewel.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Majestic Radiance Bodhisattva, the birth of jewel empowerment called the Vajra Samādhi, the Light-Samaya of All Tathāgatas, which is the heart of all Tathāgatas; it emerged from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajra-teja" emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became a great solar disc.
Having emerged, they enter the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and coalesce into a single entity, manifesting as the form of a great vajra sun that abides within the Buddha’s palm.

From that vajra-sun disc, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, emitting the light of all Tathāgatas and performing the miraculous displays of all Buddhas. Because of their supreme majesty and because the Vajrasattva samādhi is most firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahātejas. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous is the peerless light, Illuminating the realm of sentient beings;
It can purify those who are already pure— The Buddhas, the saviors of the world.”

Then, the body of that Bodhisattva Vimalamahātejas descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place upon the lunar disc to the right of all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the vajra-samādhi called the Empowerment of the Circular Radiance of All Tathāgatas, receiving the samaya of the light of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of providing incomparable light to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of bringing peace and joy to all, and even for the sake of attaining the supreme siddhi of the self-radiance of all Tathāgatas, he placed the Vajra Sun into the two hands of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahātejas.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajraprabha—bestowed the Vajraprabha empowerment. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprabha illuminated all the Tathāgatas with that Vajrasūrya light and uttered this udāna:
“This is the light of all Buddhas, Which can destroy the darkness of ignorance.
Even if there were suns as numerous as motes of dust, This light would surpass them all.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu, giving rise to the precious empowerment known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya that Fulfills the Wishes of All Tathāgatas; it is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas and issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajra-hetu" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara manifested in the form of various colored banners and streamers as ornaments.

Having emerged, they entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and condensed into a single body, taking the form of a Vajradhvaja (Vajra Banner), which remained within the Buddha’s palm.

From that Vajradhvaja form, there issued forth bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds; they erected the precious banners of all Tathāgatas and performed the miraculous displays of all Buddhas. Because it is a Great Jewel Banner and because the Vajrasattva-samādhi is extremely firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnadhvaja. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous is the peerless banner, Which accomplishes all benefit!”
"May all whose intentions are fulfilled have all their vows fulfilled.

Then, the body of that Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and took his place upon the lunar disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas, whereupon he again requested further instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the vajra-samādhi named "The Establishment and Empowerment of All Tathāgatas," which is the King of Mani-Banners for Contemplation of All Tathāgatas capable of Establishing the Samaya. For the sake of fulfilling all aspirations and bringing joy and peace to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and even until the attainment of the supreme siddhi-fruit of the great benefit of all Tathāgatas, he then placed that Vajradhvaja into the two hands of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnadhvaja.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra-name—known as Vajradhvaja—at the time of the Vajradhvaja consecration, established all the Tathāgatas in the dānapāramitā by means of the Vajradhvaja, and uttered this udāna:
"This is the state of all Buddhas, Which can fulfill all desires;
It is called the Contemplation of the Jewel Banner, And is the principle of the perfection of giving."

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Constant Joy, giving rise to the precious empowerment known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya of the Joy of All Tathāgatas, which is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas; it emerged from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajrahasa" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara smiled at all the Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and condensed into a single essence, taking the form of the Vajra-Laughter (*vajrahāsa*) and abiding within the Buddha’s palm.

From that form of the Vajra-Laughter, there issued forth bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, performing the marvelous deeds of all Tathāgatas and the miraculous play (*vikrīḍita*) of all Buddhas. Because his faculty of constant joy is supreme and because the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva is extremely firm, they condensed into a single essence, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Constant Joy-Faculty (*nityapramuditendriya*), who abided in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and uttered this *udāna*:
"How marvelous! My great laughter, The most excellent and great marvel!"
"Establishing the benefit of the Buddhas, abiding eternally in sublime meditative absorption.

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Constant Joy Root descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place upon the lunar disc behind all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the *samādhi* named Vajra of the Extraordinary Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, receiving the *samaya* of the manifestation of all Tathāgatas. For the sake of providing supreme bliss and satisfaction to all faculties throughout the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and until the attainment of the fruit of the supernormal power of the pure wisdom of the faculties of all Tathāgatas, he then bestowed that Vajra Smile with both hands upon the Great Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Constantly Joyful Faculty.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajrarati—and at the time of the Vajrarati consecration, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrarati gladdened all the Tathāgatas with a vajra smile and uttered this udāna:
“This is the manifestation of all Buddhas; How marvelous!
It displays the appearance of great joy, Which no other teacher can know.”
Mahābhiṣeka, Anuvimālaprabha, Sattva, Mahārtha, Mahāhāsa... all such as these are the Tathāgata Mahābhiṣekasattvas.

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; from it emerged the empowerment of the Dharma, the vajra-samādhi named "The Samaya of the Dharma of All Tathāgatas," which is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas, and it issued forth from his own heart.

As soon as "Vajradharma" emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara, through his perfect realization of the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena which is the purity of intrinsic nature, became the light of the True Dharma through the samādhi of Vajrasattva.

Having emerged, he illuminated all worlds with the radiance of that True Dharma, making them into the Dharma-realm; then, pervading the entire Dharma-realm, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and merged into a single essence. Measuring as vast as the void of the Dharma-realm, he took the form of a great lotus flower and rested within the palm of the Buddha.

From that vajra-lotus form, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerged; performing all miraculous displays through the samādhi-wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas, and because of their sublime mastery over all worlds and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! My ultimate reality, Primordially pure and spontaneous, All phenomena are like the raft parable— Pure and thus attainable."
Then the body of that Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, rested upon the moon-disc before all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Samādhi-Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the samādhi named Vajra, which is able to purify all Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.

In order to purify all beings and bring them peace, happiness, and joy, and ultimately to attain the fruit of the supernatural powers of the Dharma-knowledge of all Tathāgatas, he bestowed that Vajra-lotus upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Wheel-turning King of the True Dharma, and conferred the empowerment of the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas by sprinkling it upon his two hands.

Then, when all the Tathāgatas bestow the vajra-name—namely, the name Vajranetra—at the time of the Vajranetra empowerment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra, like a vajra-lotus in the manner of a blossoming lotus, observes that the nature of passionate attachment is pure and free from defilement.
Having observed this, he uttered this udāna:
“This is the realization of all Buddhas, Awakening to the reality of desire.
They placed their palms upon my hand, And established the Dharma within the Dharma.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, giving rise to the empowerment of the Dharma known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Great Wisdom Samaya of all Tathāgatas; it is called the Heart of all Tathāgatas, and he brought it forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajratīkṣṇa" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became a multitude of wisdom-swords.
Having emerged, it entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and condensed into a single entity, taking the form of a vajra-sword and abiding within the Buddha’s palm.

Then, from that vajra-sword form, there issued forth bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds; through the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, they performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas. Because of the excellence of Mañjuśrī and because the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva is extremely firm, they condensed into a single entity, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous are all Buddhas! My name is Subtle Sound.”
"Because wisdom is formless, sound can be perceived.

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and took his place upon the lunar disc to the right of all the Tathāgatas, again requesting instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, named the Vajra-Samādhi that Severs the Fetters of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of exhausting the realm of sentient beings without remainder, severing all suffering, and bestowing all peace, bliss, and joy; and for the sake of attaining the perfect accomplishment of the wisdom that accords with the voices of all Tathāgatas, he then placed that vajra-sword into the two hands of the Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajramati—when conferring the Vajramati empowerment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramati brandished and struck with a vajra sword, and uttered this udāna:
“This is the principle of the perfection of wisdom of all Buddhas;
It can sever all enemies and adversaries, And is the most supreme for eliminating all sins.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadyaścittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, giving rise to the empowerment of the Dharma known as the Vajrasamādhi Samaya of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas; called the Heart of All Tathāgatas, it emerged from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajra-hetu" emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

Having emerged from the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas, it entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and condensed into a single essence, taking the form of a vajra-wheel and abiding within the Buddha’s palm.

From that vajra-wheel form, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerged; because they had turned the wheel of Dharma upon merely generating the thought of enlightenment, and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is exceedingly firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadyo-mañjuśrī (Sadyo-vajracakra), who dwelt within the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous is the Vajra-Wheel! I, the Vajra-Holder Supreme, By the mere generation of the thought of enlightenment, Am able to turn the sublime Wheel of Dharma.”

At that moment, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Citta-pravartana-dharmacakra emerged from the heart of the World-Honored One, rested upon the lunar disc to the left of all Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the wheel of all Tathāgatas, named the Vajra Samādhi, the Great Maṇḍala Samaya of all Tathāgatas. In order to cause the entire realm of sentient beings without exception to enter and attain the non-retrogressive Wheel of Dharma, to receive all peace, bliss, and joy, and even to turn the supreme siddhi of the True Wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas, he then bestowed that Vajra-wheel upon both hands of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva *Cittotpāda-dharmacakra-pravartana*.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—known as Vajramaṇḍala—at the time of the Vajramaṇḍala consecration, had that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramaṇḍala establish all the Tathāgatas in non-retrogression by means of that vajra-wheel, and uttered this udāna:
“This is the state of all Buddhas, Which can purify all phenomena;
This is non-retrogression, And is also called the Bodhimaṇḍa.”

At that time, the Bhagavat again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vāgīśvara, giving rise to the empowerment of the Dharma known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya of the Recitation of All Tathāgatas, called the Heart of All Tathāgatas, which issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajra-bhāṣa" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi became the dharma-syllables of all the Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, they enter the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and coalesce into a single entity, taking the form of Vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*). They abide within the palm of the Buddha.

From that form of Vajra-recitation, there emerge bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, as well as the Dharma-nature of all Tathāgatas. Because they perform the wondrous speech of the supernatural play (*ṛddhivikrīḍita*) of all Buddhas, and because the *Vajrasattva-samādhi* is exceedingly firm, they coalesce into a single entity and give birth to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he utters this udāna:
"How marvelous! The natural secret; I am named Secret Speech."
"The subtle Dharma that has been taught is far removed from all conceptual proliferation.
At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vāgīśvara descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and remained upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the samādhi called the Vajra-Samādhi of the Wisdom-Samaya of the Speech of All Tathāgatas, which is the secret speech of all Tathāgatas. In order to bring about the accomplishment of speech for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, to cause them to receive all peace, happiness, and joy, and even to attain the supreme siddhi of the secret essence of the speech of all Tathāgatas, he then placed those vajra-recitations into the two hands of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Silence.

Then, when all the Tathāgatas conferred the vajra-name—known as Vajravāk—and bestowed the Vajravāk empowerment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravāk engaged in discourse with all the Tathāgatas through that vajra-recitation and uttered this udāna:
"This is the Vajra-Recitation of all Buddhas;
For all Tathāgatas, it brings swift accomplishment of mantras."

The nature of the Vajra Dharma-knowledge, the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the great wheel-turning wisdom, the speech of all Tathāgatas, and the wisdom of the wheel-turning of conceptual proliferation—this is the Great Wisdom Sattva of all Tathāgatas.
*Vajraśekhara Sarvatathāgata-tattvasaṃgraha Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-mahātantrarāja Sūtra*, Fascicle One;
*Vajraśekhara Sarvatathāgata-tattvasaṃgraha Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-mahātantrarāja Sūtra*, Fascicle Two.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daixingshan Monastery—Great Master of Universal Wisdom, who was the Kai-fu-yi-tong-sanshi, Teci, Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and granted the title Dajian—by Imperial Decree. Part Two of the Chapter on the Extensive Ritual of the Great Maṇḍala. At that time, the Bhagavat again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas, giving rise to the empowerment of karma, known as the Vajra Samādhi of the Karma-Samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Heart of all Tathāgatas, which emerged from his own heart.

As soon as "Vajrakarma" issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, because of their thorough mastery of the wisdom of the equality of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, the Vajrasattva-samādhi emerged from the Blessed One Vajradhara as the light of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, he illuminates the entire realm of sentient beings with the light of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, becoming the *karma*-realm of all Tathāgatas.

Exhausting the entire realm of the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, it enters the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, where it gathers into a single essence, its magnitude pervading the entire realm of empty space.
Because it is the *karma*-realm of all Tathāgatas, the form of Karma-vajra arises and dwells within the palms of the Buddhas.

Then, from the form of Karma-vajra, there emerge bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, performing all Buddha-activities and supernatural displays (*ṛddhi-vikrīḍita*) throughout all worlds as the *karma* of all Tathāgatas, and because they perform the boundless activities of all Tathāgatas and because the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva is extremely firm, they gather into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Viśvakarman of all Tathāgatas. Dwelling in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he utters this udāna:
“Marvelous is the non-empty Buddha! My manifold activities are many!”
"By performing deeds without merit, one gains the benefit of Buddhahood and is able to transform adamantine karma.
At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Viśvakarman descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and stood upon a moon disc before all the Tathāgatas, once again requesting instructions.

Then the World-Honored One entered the Samaya of the Non-empty Vajra of All Tathāgatas, known as the Vajra Samādhi that Transforms All Offerings and the Like—an immeasurable, non-empty ritual procedure for all activities, vast in its Samaya—which brings about all siddhis for the realm of sentient beings without exception, bestows all peace, happiness, and joy, and even accomplishes the fruit of the supernatural powers of the vajra-karma-nature wisdom of all Tathāgatas. He then bestowed that Karma-Vajra upon the Great Bodhisattva Vajrakarma of All Tathāgatas, consecrating him with the empowerment of all Tathāgatas as the Wheel-Turning King of the Karma of All Tathāgatas, and placed it in his two hands.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra-name—known as Vajraviśva—at the time of the Vajraviśva consecration, established that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva with the Karma-vajra at his own heart, causing him to abide in the state of equality of the karma of all Tathāgatas, and spoke this udāna:
"This is the work of all Buddhas, Performing various supreme activities;
They place it within my palms, Establishing karma within karma."

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Invincible Vigor, giving rise to the empowerment of karma known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya of the Protection of All Tathāgatas, which is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas; it issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajra-rukṣa" emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became a multitude of firm armor.

Having emerged, they enter the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and merge into a single essence, taking the form of a great adamantine armor, which then abides within the Buddha’s palm.

From that form of the Vajra Armor (*vajrakaṅkaṭa*), there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, performing the vast activities of the protective rituals of all Tathāgatas and the miraculous play (*vikrīḍita*) of all Buddhas. Because his diligence was invincible and because the *samādhi* of Vajrasattva was extremely firm, they condensed into a single body, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Invincible Diligence (*Duryodhana-vīrya*). Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous is the armor of diligence! I am the one who is truly firm;
By virtue of being firm yet bodiless, I have manifested this supreme vajra-body.”

Then the body of that Great Bodhisattva Durdharṣavīrya descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place upon the lunar disc to the right of all Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the vajra-samādhi named "The Solidity of All Tathāgatas," the samaya of the Vajra-pāramitā of Diligence of All Tathāgatas. For the sake of protecting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of bestowing all peace, happiness, and joy, and even for the sake of attaining the fruit of the accomplishment of the vajra-body of all Tathāgatas, he then placed the vajra armor into the two hands of the Great Bodhisattva Invincible Diligence (Durjayavīrya).

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of a vajra name—bestowing the name Vajramaitrī—conferred the Vajramaitrī empowerment. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramaitrī donned the vajra armor for all the Tathāgatas and uttered this udāna:
“This is the supreme armor of compassion of all Buddhas;
A firm and vigorous great protection, Named ‘The Great Friend of Loving-kindness.’”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamārapramardin, giving rise to the empowerment of karma known as the Vajra Samādhi, the Samaya of the Expedient Means of all Tathāgatas, which is called the Heart of all Tathāgatas; it issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajrayakṣa" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the great fanged weapon.
Having emerged, he entered the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, and merged into a single entity, taking the form of a vajra-tooth. He remained within the palm of the Buddha.

From that vajra-tooth form, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds issued forth, performing all acts of subduing the violent and wrathful, and manifesting the miraculous play of the supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) of all Buddhas. Because they thoroughly vanquish all Māras and because the *vajrasattva-samādhi* is extremely firm, they merged into a single entity, giving rise to the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin. Abiding in the heart of the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, he uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! The great skillful means, The compassion of all Buddhas!"
"By means of the tranquility of form, he manifests in a wrathful form.

At that time, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin descended from the heart of the World-Honored One and dwelt upon the lunar disc to the left of all the Tathāgatas, again requesting instructions.

Then the World-Honored One entered the samādhi of the Vajra of Supreme Wrath of All Tathāgatas. To subdue those difficult to tame among all Tathāgatas, to bestow fearlessness upon the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, to grant them all peace, happiness, and joy, and even to attain the fruit of the most supreme siddhi—the supernormal powers and the great wisdom of skillful means of all Tathāgatas—he then bestowed that weapon of the Vajra Fang upon the two hands of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—Vajracaṇḍa—during the consecration of Vajracaṇḍa, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracaṇḍa placed that vajra-tooth weapon in his own mouth and, terrifying all the Tathāgatas, uttered this udāna:
“This is the [weapon] of all Buddhas, The subduer of those difficult to subdue;
The vajra-tooth weapon, The skillful means of compassionate mercy.”

At that time, the Bhagavān again entered the samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Fist of All Tathāgatas, giving rise to the empowerment of karma known as the Vajra Samādhi of the Vajra Bond of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas; it is called the Heart of All Tathāgatas and issued forth from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajrasandi" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the seal-binding (mudrā-bandha) of all the Tathāgatas.

Having emerged, they enter the heart of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and merge into a single entity, taking the form of the Vajra-Bond; they abide within the Buddha’s palm, and from that Vajra-Bond form, bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerge.

Having emerged, they perform all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas through the wisdom of the seal-binding (*mudrā-bandhana*) and so forth of all Tathāgatas in all worlds. Because they have skillfully bound the fists of all Tathāgatas and because the *Vajrasattva-samādhi* is extremely firm, they merge into a single body, giving rise to the form of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi. Abiding in the heart of the Bhagavān Vairocana Buddha, he utters this udāna:
"How marvelous! This wondrous and firm bond, I am the firm samaya;
Because it fulfills all aspirations, The liberated are bound."

Then the body of that Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi descended from the heart of the World-Honored One, took his place upon the lunar disc behind all the Tathāgatas, and again requested instruction.

Then the World-Honored One entered the samaya of all Tathāgatas, named the Vajra Samādhi Samaya of the Seals of All Tathāgatas. In order to cause the manifestation and verification of all siddhis for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, to bestow all peace, bliss, and joy, and even to attain the sovereign fruit of the supreme siddhi of the seal of the omniscient wisdom of all Tathāgatas, he then bestowed that vajra-bind upon the hands of the Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi of All Tathāgatas.

Then all those Tathāgatas, by means of the vajra name—known as Vajramuṣṭi—at the time of the Vajramuṣṭi empowerment, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi bound all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-bind and uttered this udāna:
“This is the seal-binding of all Buddhas, Greatly firm and solid;
because it swiftly accomplishes all seals, One does not transgress the samaya.”

The vast ritual procedures for making offerings to all Tathāgatas; the great diligence and firm armor of all Tathāgatas; the great skillful means of all Tathāgatas; the wisdom of all seals and bonds of all Tathāgatas... such as these are the Great Karma-sattvas of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, after the Tathāgata Acala had accomplished the wisdom of all Tathāgatas for the World-Honored One Vairocana, and having sealed the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, he entered the *vajrapāramitā-samaya* and gave rise to the vajra empowerment known as the *vajrasamādhi*, the *samaya* of all Tathāgatas. This is called the Seal of All Tathāgatas, which emerged from his own heart.
As soon as "Sattvavajri" emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, vajra-light radiated forth.
From that gateway of vajra-light, the Blessed One Vajradhara manifested as bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, and sealed all Tathāgatas with their wisdom.

They again merge into a single body, equal in measure to all worlds, and manifest as the form of the Great Vajra. Abiding upon the moon disc before the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, they utter this udāna:
"O wonder! All Buddhas, Sattva-vajra is firm;
Because of that firmness and the absence of body, One attains the vajra-body."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to seal the World-Honored One Vairocana with the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, entered the samaya of the Jewel Pāramitā. From his own heart there emerged the empowerment of the jewel-vajra born thereof, named the Vajra Samādhi Vajra Samaya, which is called the Self-Seal.
As soon as "Ratnavajri" had issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, jewel-like light radiated forth.
From that jewel-light, the Blessed One Vajradhara manifested as bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, sealing all Tathāgatas with wisdom.

Again, they gather into a single body, equal in measure to all worlds, and take the form of a great vajra-jewel. It abides upon the lunar disc to the right of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and utters this udāna:
"How marvelous, all Buddhas! I am named Ratnavajra;
Among all the assemblies of mudrās, I am the firm principle of empowerment."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to seal the wisdom of all Tathāgatas of the World-Honored One Vairocana, entered the samaya of the Dharma-pāramitā. From his own heart, there emerged the empowerment of the Dharma-vajra born thereof, known as the Vajra-samādhi-dharma-samaya, and named the Self-Seal (svamudrā).
As soon as "Dharmavajri" had issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, lotus-light rays emerged.

From those lotus-light rays, that very Bhagavat Vajradhara manifested the body-seals (*kāyamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, and [bestowed] the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

They again merge into a single entity, equal in size to all worlds, and manifest in the form of a great vajra-lotus. It abides upon the lunar disc behind the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha and utters this udāna:
“Marvelous are all Buddhas! The Dharma-vajra is my purity;
By virtue of its intrinsic purity, It renders even lustful passion stainless.”

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, in order to seal Vairocana with the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, entered the samaya of all pāramitās. From his own heart there emerged the vajra empowerment born thereof, called the Vajra Samādhi of All Samayas, which is named the Self-Seal (svamudrā).
As soon as “Karmavajri” had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, all the light of karma emerged.

From that light of the karma of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the bodies of the Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms of all worlds, and pervasively sealed the wisdom of all the Tathāgatas.

Once again, they gather into a single body, equal in measure to all worlds and facing in all directions, manifesting as the Great Karma-Vajra form. Abiding upon the lunar disc to the left of the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, he utters this udāna:
“Marvelous are all Buddhas! I am named Karma-Vajra;
From one, I become all, Performing the wholesome deeds of the Buddha-realm.”
The great empowerment of the wisdom-samaya of all Tathāgatas, the vajra-dharmatā of all offerings—such is the great pāramitā of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Vairocana Buddha, again entered the samaya of the joyful offering of all Tathāgatas; from this arose the vajra-samādhi named "Born of All Tathāgata Families," and the Great Goddesses of the families of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart.
Upon the mere emergence of "Vajralāsyā" from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra-mudrā appeared.
From that gateway of the Vajra-mudrā, the Blessed One Vajradhara became the bodies of as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all worlds.

Once again, they gathered into a single body as the Great Goddess Vajralāsyā, like a Vajrasattva, possessing the nature of all bodies, various forms and colors, and all modes of deportment; she encompassed all the Vajrasattvīs of the Tathāgata families and dwelt upon the lunar disc to the left of the mandala of the World-Honored One Acala Tathāgata, uttering this udāna:
“Marvelous! Peerless! The offering among all Buddhas;
Through the offering of passionate attachment, One is able to transform all offerings.”

At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana again entered the samaya of the consecration by the jewel-garland of all Tathāgatas; from this, the samādhi named Vajra was produced, and the Great Goddesses of the families of all Tathāgatas emerged from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajramale" issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, the Great Jewel Seal emerged.
From that Great Jewel Seal, the Blessed One Vajradhara became the bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

They again gathered into a single body as the Great Goddess Vajramālā, and abiding upon the moon disc to the left of the maṇḍala of the World-Honored One Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, she uttered this udāna:
“Marvelous! I am peerless, Renowned as Ratnapūjā;
To the Victorious King of the Three Realms, I offer worship at his command.”

At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana again entered the samaya of the song-offering of all Tathāgatas, which gives rise to the vajra-samādhi named "The Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas," who then emerged from his own heart.
"Vajra-ṇṛtye. As soon as this had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Dharma-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas emerged.
From those seals of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the bodies of as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all worlds.

These then condensed into a single form as the Great Goddess Vajragītā, and she dwelt upon the moon disc to the left of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, and uttered this udāna:
“O wonder! Accomplished in song, I make offerings to all who see!”
"By means of this offering, all phenomena resonate like echoes.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called "Vajra" produced by the dance-offering of all Tathāgatas; from his own heart, the Great Goddesses of the families of all Tathāgatas emerged.
"Vajranṛtye. As soon as this emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the vast ritual of the dance of all the Tathāgatas issued forth.
From that emerged the ritual for the dance offering of all Tathāgatas; then the Blessed One Vajradhara became the bodies of as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all worlds.
They again merge into a single body as the Great Goddess Vajranṛtyā, who dwells upon the moon disk to the left of the World-Honored One Akṣobhyavajra Tathāgata, and utters this udāna:
“O wonder! Through vast offerings, and for the sake of performing all offerings, by means of the rite of the Vajra Dance, the offering to the Buddha is established.”

The samaya of the unsurpassed bliss and delight of all Tathāgatas, the garland of all Tathāgatas, the chanting of all Tathāgatas, the unsurpassed performance of the act of making offerings of all Tathāgatas... such are the secret offerings of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, in order to respond to the offering of the Tathāgata Vairocana, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, entered the samādhi called the Vajra Samādhi produced from the Pledge of the Ability to Delight All Tathāgatas; from his own heart, the female servants of all Tathāgatas emerged.

As soon as "Vajradhūpe" issued forth from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajrapāṇi manifested in various forms, adorned with clouds of incense and offerings, pervading the entire Vajradhātu.
Having emerged, from that ocean-like cloud of incense offerings, there appeared bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds.

These then merged into a single entity, becoming the body of the Vajra Incense Goddess (Vajradhūpā), and she took her place upon a moon disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajra-maṇi-jewel-peak pavilion, reciting this udāna:
"How marvelous is the great offering! It is refreshing, radiant, and perfectly adorned."
"By means of the universal entry of the *sattva*, one swiftly realizes awakening.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to respond to the offering of the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the *samaya* of the Jewel-Adorned Offering. From his own heart there emerged the Great Goddess named Vajrasamādhi, who is the command of all Tathāgatas.

“Vajrapuṣpe. As soon as this [mantra] issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the adornment of offerings of all flowers, pervading and filling the entire realm of space.
Having emerged, from that array of offerings of all flowers, there issued forth bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, they again condensed into a single form, taking the shape of the Vajra-flower Goddess (Vajrapuṣpadevī). She dwelt upon a moon disc at the left corner of the Tathāgata’s Vajramaṇiratna-śikhara pavilion and uttered this udāna:
“O wonderful offering of flowers, Which is able to create all adornments!”
"By means of the Tathāgata-jewel-nature, one swiftly obtains offerings.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja, in order to respond to the World-Honored One Vairocana’s offering, entered the samaya of the light-offering of all Tathāgatas; from this arose the vajra-samādhi named "The Birth," and the female messengers of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart.

As soon as "Vajraloke" issued from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara manifested an array of offerings consisting of all realms of light, which extended throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm; from those ornaments of all realms of light, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds.

Having emerged, they again gathered into a single body, taking the form of the Vajraprabhā-devī. She dwelt upon a moon disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion and uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! My vastness is great; Through the offering of lamps, she is most sublime.
By swiftly possessing radiant light, She attains the eye of all Buddhas."

At that time, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, in order to respond to the offering made by the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samaya of the ointment-offering of all Tathāgatas; from this arose the vajra-samādhi named "Born of All Tathāgatas," and the female servants of all Tathāgatas issued forth from his own heart.

As soon as "Vajragandhe" emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara produced all manner of ointment offerings and ornaments, which pervaded the entire Dharma-realm; from those ointment offerings and ornaments, bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds emerged.

Having emerged, they again gathered into a single body, becoming the body of the Vajra-gandhā-devī. She dwelt upon a moon disc at the left corner of the World-Honored One’s Vajra-maṇi-ratna-śikhara-paṇḍita-kūṭāgāra, and uttered this udāna:
“Wonderful is this fragrant offering, Subtle and delightful to me;
By virtue of the Tathāgata’s fragrance, It is bestowed upon all bodies.”

The Samaya of the Great Bodhi-limb through which the Wisdom of all Tathāgatas Pervasively Enters; the Light, Precepts, Concentration, Wisdom, Liberation, and Knowledge and Vision of Liberation of all Tathāgatas; the Incense... and so forth, these are the female messengers who receive the instructions of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata, again entered the Samaya Hook Samādhi of all Tathāgatas; from his own heart there emerged the Lord of the Multitude of All Seals of All Tathāgatas, the Being born of the Samādhi named Vajra.

As soon as "Vajra-kuśa" issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Blessed One Vajradhara produced the entire host of seals (*mudrā*) of all the Tathāgatas; and from that host of seals of all the Tathāgatas, there emerged bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

They again merged into a single body, becoming the Great Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa, and dwelt within the moon disc at the vajra gate of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, summoning the samayas of all Tathāgatas and uttering this udāna:
“O wonder! All Buddhas, My hook-vow is firm;
By my universal summoning, All maṇḍalas are assembled.”

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samaya of all Tathāgatas and was introduced into the Mahāsattva-samaya; from his own heart there emerged the Vajra-samādhi named "Seal-Entry of All Tathāgatas Accepting the Command."

As soon as "Vajrapāśa" issued forth from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara brought forth from the assembly of the Samaya-entrance-invoking mudrās of all Tathāgatas bodies of Tathāgatas equal in number to the atoms of all worlds.

Once again, they merge into a single body, becoming the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa. He dwells within the moon disc at the gateway of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, and having summoned all the Tathāgatas, he utters this udāna:
“O wonder, all Buddhas! I am the firm Vajrapāśa.
Even if one enters into all atoms, I shall draw them back in here.”

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samaya of the Great Sattva Lock of all Tathāgatas, which arises from the Vajra-samādhi named the Samaya of all Tathāgatas; he bound all Tathāgatas and caused [the mantra] to issue forth from his own heart.

As soon as "Vajrasphoṭa" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara produced the seal-mass of the samaya-bonds of all the Tathāgatas from that seal-mass of the samaya-bonds of all the Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, he manifested bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

These then reassembled into a single body, that of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasaṃhata, and dwelt upon the lunar disc within the Dharma-gate of the Lord’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion, uttering this udāna:
"O wonder! All Buddhas, The great, firm Vajrasaṃhata!"
"Those who cause all bonds to be released, bind themselves for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.

At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatāveśa, from which there emerged the Vajrasamādhi named "All-Seal Servant of All Tathāgatas," arising from his own heart.
As soon as "Vajravesha" had issued from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became the Lord of Seals for all the Tathāgatas.
Having emerged, from that Lord of Seals (*mudrāpati*) of all Tathāgatas, there issued forth bodies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds.

These then gathered back into a single body, becoming the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasamāveśa. He dwelt within the lunar disc at the gate of activity (*karmadvāra*) of the World-Honored One’s Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion and uttered this udāna:
“O wonder! All Buddhas, I, firm vajra, have entered!”
"One becomes the sovereign of all, and yet also becomes a servant.
This is the command of all Tathāgatas: the summoning, the leading in, the binding, and the subduing through the samaya-hook of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, for the purpose of summoning all Tathāgatas, the World-Honored One made the gesture of the vajra-snap of the fingers and spoke this heart-mantra for the empowerment of summoning all Tathāgatas:

"Vajrasamāja. In an instant, a *kṣaṇa*, or a *lava*, or a *muhūrta*, after all Tathāgatas had been awakened by the gesture of the vajra-snap of the fingers, there assembled from throughout the ocean-like clouds of all worlds, as numerous as the atoms within all worlds, all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas in the maṇḍala of the assembly.
Having assembled, they proceeded to the Vajramaṇiratnaśikhara Pavilion where the Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata was staying.
Upon arrival, they uttered this heart-mantra for prostrating at the feet of all Tathāgatas:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapraṇāmanena karomi. Having thus prostrated to all Tathāgatas by reciting this *svabhāvasiddhi-mantra* according to their intention, they spoke this udāna:
"How marvelous! This is the majestic deportment of the Bodhisattva Mahāsamantabhadra;
it is the maṇḍala-cakra of the Tathāgata, manifested as the reflection of the Tathāgata.

When the Tathāgatas assembled from all the worlds of the ten directions had thus spoken, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, the entire maṇḍala of the assembly of Bodhisattvas entered the heart of the Buddha Vairocana.

Having emerged from the hearts of all those Tathāgatas as individual maṇḍalas of their respective bodhisattva assemblies, they dwelt in the samādhi of constructing a maṇḍala surrounding the World-Honored One Vairocana’s Vajra-maṇi-peak Pavilion, and uttered this udāna:
"How marvelous! All Buddhas, vast and without beginning, through the number of all atoms, have attained the single nature of Buddhahood."

At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgatas of all [families], again assembled. In order to empower the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, to rescue and provide all benefit and happiness for the realm of sentient beings without exception, and even to achieve the supreme accomplishment of the sameness-wisdom, supernormal powers, and perfect enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, they invoked the Blessed One, the Sovereign of all Tathāgatas, Vajrasattva, the Great Vajradhara without beginning or end, with these one hundred and eight verses of praise:
“O Great Mind of Vajra Hero, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, Samantabhadra, Primordial Vajra— I pay homage to you, Vajrapāṇi!”
Vajrarāja Subuddhi, Vajrāṅkuśa Tathāgata,
Amogharāja Vajra— I pay homage to Vajrākarṣaṇa;
Vajrarāga Mahāsukha, Vajraśara who subdues all.
Māyājāla-mahāvajra, I pay homage to Vajracāpa;
Vajrasattva, the virtuous, Vajralāsa, the great delight,
Ratnavajra, the King of Joy— I pay homage to Vajrarati.
Vajraratna-vajra, Vajra-śūnyatā-mahāratna,
Ratnagarbha-vajra-śikhara— I pay homage to Vajragarbha;
Vajratejas-mahājvāla, Vajrasūrya-buddhaprabha.
Vajra Light of Great Majesty, I pay homage to Vajra Light;
Vajra Banner of Excellent Benefit, Vajra Pennant of Sublime Joy,
Jewel Banner, Great Vajra, I pay homage to Vajra Realm.
Vajra-laughter, great laughter; Vajra-laughter, most marvelous.
Supreme Vajra-love and joy, I pay homage to Vajra-love.
Vajra-dharma, excellent benefit; Vajra-lotus, wondrous purity.
World-honored One, Vajra Eye, I pay homage to the Vajra Eye;
Vajra of the sharp Mahāyāna, Vajra sword and weapon,
Sublime and auspicious Vajra Passion, I pay homage to Vajra Wisdom.
The great field of the Vajra Cause, the principle of the Vajra Wheel,
which can turn and give rise to the Vajra— I pay homage to the Vajra Field.
The Vajra Speech of wondrous clarity, the Vajra Recitation of wondrous accomplishment.
The accomplishment of the Wordless Vajra—homage to the Vajra Speech;
The Vajra Action Command—Amoghasiddhi, the Vajra of Vast Activity;
The Vajra of Pervasive Action—homage to the Vajra Skillfulness.
Vajrapāṇi, the Great Hero; Vajra Armor, the Great Firm One;
Incomparable and Sublime Diligence—I pay homage to Vajravīrya;
Vajra Exhaustion of Expedients; Vajradaṃṣṭra, the Great Terrifier.
Vajra of the steep destruction of Māras, I pay homage to Vajra-krodha;
Vajra of majestic and awe-inspiring command, Vajra capable of binding and releasing,
Vajra-muṣṭi of supreme vows, I pay homage to Vajra-muṣṭi.
If there be one who holds these names, The hundred-and-eightfold hymn of tranquility,
And the vajra-name consecration, They too shall obtain such [attainments].
If there be one who, by means of these names, Praises the Great Vajradhara,
Those who chant with right intention are like those who hold a vajra.
By means of these names, this hymn of one hundred and eight names,
may the Mahāyāna be realized and its vast principles flow everywhere.
“We praise you, O Venerable One; we pray that you will explain the most excellent rite—the Great Wheel of all Buddhas, the supreme great maṇḍala.

Then, the Blessed One, the Great Vajradhara, having heard the request of all the Tathāgatas, entered the vajra-samādhi empowered by the birth from the samaya of all the Tathāgatas, and spoke the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu:
"Next, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala,
which is like the Vajradhātu and is named the Vajradhātu.
One should sit in the maṇḍala according to the instructions."
One should contemplate and empower the Great Seal of the Mahāsattva.
Abiding in the seal, one should arise, survey all directions,
and stride with haughty majesty while reciting the mantra of Vajrasattva.
With new thread, join it well; according to measure, make it dignified.
Using the wisdom of the thread, one should mark out the maṇḍala according to one's capacity.
It should have four sides with four gates, adorned with four boundary-markers.
With four lines intersecting and interlacing, adorned with garlands of silk and brocade;
at every corner and where the gates meet,
inlaid with vajra-jewels— one should mark out the outer wheel-maṇḍala.
Within that, in the shape of a wheel, one should enter the central palace;
it is completely marked with vajra-lines and adorned with eight pillars.
Upon the supreme vajra-pillars, one should decorate the mandala of the five wheels.
Within that maṇḍala, one should establish the image of the Buddha.
Surrounding the Buddha on all sides, within the maṇḍala,
one should draw the four supreme samayas in their proper sequence.
Advancing with the vajra-step, within the four maṇḍalas,
one should establish all the Buddhas, such as Akṣobhya and the others.
One should construct the Acala maṇḍala, [offering] to Vajradhara and the rest.
The maṇḍala of Ratnasaṃbhava is filled with Vajragarbha and the others;
the maṇḍala of Amitāyus, the wheel of pure karma of Vajranetra;
one should likewise draw the maṇḍalas of Amoghasiddhi, Vajraviśva, and the rest.
Established at the corners of the wheel, one should paint the Vajra-women;
in the corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should paint the Buddha-offerings.
In all places within the gates, the four classes of gate-protectors should be depicted.
Established within the outer maṇḍala, one should paint the Mahāsattvas.
This is the supreme samaya: forming the mudrās according to the ritual rules, the Vajra Master enters;
having entered, he destroys the seals and pervades everywhere.
Regarding these *sarvavisa* (all-pervading) mantras:
having performed the commands according to the original teachings, such as the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*) and so forth,
one should recite one's own name and achieve [the state] through the vajra.
The Sattvavajra Hook—the Vajra Master then binds it;
making the beckoning gesture with a snap of the fingers, one should invite all Buddhas.
In an instant, all the Buddhas, together with Vajrasattva, [arrive].
One should fill all the maṇḍalas and assemble the mandala.
Then, with the swift Great Seal, one should visualize Vajrasattva;
by reciting the hundred and eight [names] once, one rejoices through this assembly.
The Tathāgatas are all firm and solid; the Vajrasattvas are self-perfected.
Abiding as compassionate friends, they perform their activities with the hooks and other implements at every gate and in all places.
