Abiding in the samaya, through the seal-samaya of the Sattva-vajra and others, one should become a Mahāsattva.
By reciting JAḤ HŪṂ BAṂ HOḤ, one becomes equal to all.
Having summoned the Great Sattvas, having drawn them in with the hook,
bound them, and subdued them, one should then perform secret offerings to cause those of great majesty to rejoice.
For the benefit of sentient beings,
may all things be accomplished; such are the activities of the Vajra Master within these various maṇḍalas.
The Vajraśekhara Sarvatathāgata-tattvasaṃgraha Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-mahākalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Middle;
The Vajraśekhara Sarvatathāgata-tattvasaṃgraha Mahāyāna-abhisamaya-mahākalparāja Sūtra, Scroll Lower.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daixingshan Monastery—Great Master of Universal Wisdom, Grand Preceptor, posthumously titled Minister of Works, invested with the purple robe, granted the title of Duke of Sui with a fief of three thousand households, and holding the rank of Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si, Te-jin, and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial—by Imperial Decree. Chapter Three: The Extensive Ritual for the Great Maṇḍala. Next, the ritual procedure for the entry of the Vajra-disciples into the Great Vajra Maṇḍala shall be explained in detail.

Within this context, I have first explained that because one enters this great maṇḍala for the sake of the supreme siddhi—the cause and fruit of bringing all sentient beings without exception into the state of exhaustion, and of rescuing, benefiting, and bringing them peace and happiness—one should not discriminate between those who are fit vessels and those who are not.
Why is this? World-Honored One!

There may be sentient beings who have committed great transgressions; yet if they enter this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, having seen it and entered it, they will be freed from all evil destinies.
“World-Honored One!

There may be sentient beings who are stained by attachment to various gains, food, and drink, and who detest the samaya; for those who, as practitioners of preliminary rites and the like, enter according to their own inclinations and preferences, they shall then obtain the fulfillment of all their wishes.”

“Bhagavān! There may be sentient beings who delight in song, dance, play, food, drink, and amusements; because they do not understand the nature of reality (*dharmatā*) as realized through the Mahāyāna by all Tathāgatas, they enter the maṇḍalas of other classes of devas, where they find supreme gratification in the fulfillment of all their desires and give rise to love, delight, and joy.”

Those who do not enter out of fear of the prohibitions of the maṇḍala of the family of all Tathāgatas will find themselves entering the gateway to the path of the maṇḍalas of the evil destinies; therefore, they should enter this Great Vajradhātu Maṇḍala. This is for the sake of causing all to experience the supreme siddhi of well-being, joy, and satisfaction, and because it can transform the manifest path of all evil destinies.
“World-Honored One!

Furthermore, there are sentient beings who abide in the True Dharma; for the sake of all sentient beings seeking the most supreme siddhi of the precepts, concentration, and wisdom of all Tathāgatas, as well as the skillful means of Buddha-bodhi, they have long cultivated dhyāna, liberation, the stages [of the bodhisattva], and so forth, and thus they have become weary.”
Upon entering this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, as soon as one has entered, even the fruition of all Tathāgatas is not difficult to attain, let alone other types of siddhi.
Next, one should first perform the fourfold prostration to all the Tathāgatas. Extending the arms fully with vajra-palms joined, touch the ground with the chest and prostrate toward the east.

The mantra is: *Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāya tmanā nirayāntaye sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhiṣṭhasva māṃ*. Then, keeping the aforementioned vajra-palms at the heart, touch the ground with the forehead and prostrate toward the south. The mantra is:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāviśodhaye tmanan niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajraratna viṣṭaram. Then, with the same previous vajra-palms placed at the head, touch the ground with the mouth and pay homage to the west;

the mantra is: "Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpramardana tmanan niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajradharma pramardanaya. Then, with the same previous vajra-palms at the heart, touch the ground with the crown of the head and pay homage to the north; the mantra is:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmāṇi ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrakarma kuru māṃ. Then, having the disciple wear a crimson silk shawl across the shoulder and cover the face with crimson cloth, have the disciple form the Sattvavajra mudrā with this heart-mantra:
"Samayas tvam. Then, having them hold a flower garland with the two middle fingers, cause them to enter the samaya with this heart-mantra: "Hūṃ."
Having entered, he speaks these words:
"Anīya-satvaṃ sarvatathāgataguhyaprativiṣṭa-sattvānām hṛdi vajrajñā..."

*Nṛṣṭha-mahāmaṇḍala-vyakta-vijaya-mati-samayodyata-nitī* (The Great Maṇḍala of the Victorious Manifestation of the Supreme Being).
The Vajrācārya himself should form the Sattvavajra mudrā,
place it upon the crown of the disciple’s head, and perform this:
He says:
"This is the Samaya-vajra; it shall crush your head if you speak [of this].
He empowers the oath-water once and causes the disciple to drink the oath-water, with the mantra as follows:
"Vajrasattva sarvajñatāṃ me hrīṇaye samayas tiṣṭha dṛḍhībhava mā me pādau niṣīda sādhukṣaṇam adya te niyamo nirmala yan vajranāthas tvām ājñāpayati. Then he says to the disciple:
"From this day forward, you shall regard me as Vajrapāṇi."
"What I should tell you, you must do accordingly.
You should not treat me with contempt; lest you invite calamity and, after death, fall into hell."

Having spoken these words, one should pray: "May all Tathāgatas grant their empowerment; may Vajrasattva enter everywhere into the Vajrācārya. One should then form the Sattvavajra-mudrā and speak as follows:

*ĀRYA SAMAYA PRABHŪTA VAJRASATTVA MĪTI SAMITIDAM AVIŚAYA TUṬYE VAJRAKIRĪṬANA MAHĀNUTTARA VAJRAVEŚA AḤ.* Then, having formed the Wrathful Fist (krodhamuṣṭi) and the Sattvavajra-mudrā, and employing the Vajra-speech as desired, one should recite the Hundred-Syllable Mantra of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya. This constitutes the *aviśaya*.

As soon as he has performed the *avaśeṣa*, a subtle and wondrous wisdom arises; by means of this, he knows the minds of others, realizes the minds of others, and knows the three times regarding all matters. His mind then becomes firm and stable; within the teachings of all Tathāgatas, he completely eliminates all suffering and affliction, leaves behind all evil destinies, and remains unimpeded among all sentient beings. Empowered by all Tathāgatas, all *siddhis* manifest before him, and he attains that which was never before experienced, giving rise to joy, bliss, and mental satisfaction.
By means of this bliss and so forth, one may achieve samādhi, or the gates of dhāraṇī, or have all one's wishes fulfilled, even unto the achievement of the essential nature of all Tathāgatas.
Then, having bound that mudrā to release the disciple’s mind, recite this heart-mantra:
*Tiṣṭha vajra nirdhūme bhava śāśvata*.

*Vadome bhava hṛdaye me tiṣṭha sarvasiddhiñcā me prayaccha hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ.* Then, have the disciple cast the flower garland into the great maṇḍala with this heart-mantra: *Pratīccha vajra hoḥ*. Whichever deity’s location the flower falls upon, that deity will be accomplished.
Then take that flower garland and bind it upon the disciple’s head with this heart-mantra: *Oṃ pratigṛhṇa hṛdaya tvaṃ me svā mahāmāla*.
By this, the Great Being (Mahāsattva) will embrace [the practitioner], and accomplishment will be swiftly attained. Once entry has been completed, remove the face-covering with this heart-mantra:

"Oṃ vajrasattva sarvādhiṣṭhāna-ākrośa-nāgataṃ trāyoparā-unagataye ti sarvakleśavajrākrośanottaraṇi. Then, reciting the *darśana-mantra*: "Hī vajrapaśya," he causes the disciple to look at the great maṇḍala in succession.
As soon as it has been seen, all Tathāgatas empower and protect him, and Vajrasattva dwells within that disciple's heart.

Then one sees various signs of light, playful displays, and supernormal powers; through the vision of the maṇḍala and by the empowerment of the Tathāgata, one either sees the Bhagavān Mahāvajradhara manifesting his original form, or one sees the Tathāgata.
From this point forward, all aims, all desired objects, and all *siddhis* shall be attained.

Once the Vajra-holder and the Tathāgata have revealed the great maṇḍala, they shall empower a flask of fragrant water with the vajra and consecrate the disciple’s crown with it, using this heart-mantra:
*vajrāviśca*. Then, having bound a garland with a corresponding mudrā and placed their own insignia within the palms of both hands, they shall recite the heart-mantra.

“*Anīya-viṣakta-sattva-masi-mudrā-vajra-viśaktate ina-de sarva-buddha-tvaṃ kṛṣṇa-vajra-susiddhaye hūṃ vajra-dīpate tvaṃ mā viṣañca me tiṣṭha vajra-samaya-stvam.*” Then, one should confer the empowerment with the name using this heart-mantra:
“*Oṃ vajra-sattva-jñāna-viṣañca me vajra-nāma-viśaktate vajra-mama.*” If one bestows a name upon a disciple, it should be appended [to the mantra] accordingly.
Having called them forth, he extensively explains the ritual for entering all maṇḍalas, and then asks the disciples:
"Do you delight in the wisdom that brings forth siddhi?"
Is it the wisdom of the siddhi of supernatural powers?
Is it the wisdom of the siddhi of the vidyādhara?
Or is it the wisdom of the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas?
"According to their inclinations, one should teach by explaining [the teachings]; thus the seals (*mudrā*) and wisdom (*jñāna*) that accomplish the *siddhi* of meaningful benefit are realized.
Abiding in the treasury of the vajra-form, One should visualize it within the heart;
Having visualized it and established oneself upon the ground, Then one shall behold the hidden treasure."
Having visualized the vajra-form, one should look all around in the sky;
wherever it is seen to descend, that is the hidden treasure.
The wise person should likewise visualize the vajra-form upon the tongue.
Declaring, "It is here," his words become true.
Visualizing oneself as the form of Vajra, one should contemplate it entering everywhere until it descends upon that spot; that location is a treasure cache.
Their heart-mantras are:
*vajranidhi ratnanidhi dharmanidhi karmānidhi*. Next, one should instruct them in the mudrās and wisdom-knowledge for accomplishing the Vajra-siddhi.
Once the Vajra-entry has arisen, water takes on the form of a vajra;
through meditative observation, one swiftly achieves accomplishment and wanders upon the waters.
Again, the Vajra-entry arises, its bodily color identical to its own form.
Cultivating in this manner, one naturally assumes the form of a Buddha.
Pervading the entire body and contemplating that very body as empty,
once one has practiced according to one's inclination, one will attain the *ānanda*.
Entering oneself as Vajra, one should contemplate oneself as being like a vajra;
even unto leaping upward, one then attains the power of moving through space.
The mantras for these [practices] are as follows:
"Vajra-ānala vajra-rūpa vajra-kāśa vajra-mām. Next, one is instructed in the mudrā and vidyā for accomplishing the siddhi of the Vajra-vidyādhara.
"One should visualize the form of the moon, leaping upward into the void;
grasping the vajra with one's hand, one attains the Vajra-Vidyādhara.
Ascending upon the lunar disc, one should visualize the Vajra-Jewel."
One who has purified the body acts according to their desire; in an instant, they achieve the power of soaring through the air.
Having ascended upon the lunar disc, holding a vajra-lotus in hand, one should visualize the Vajra-eye;
thus, the rank of a Vidyādhara is attained.
Abiding within the lunar disc, one should visualize Karma-vajra;
by swiftly attaining vajra skillfulness, one then becomes a vidyādhara.
The heart-mantras for these and others are as follows:
“Vajradhara, Ratnadhara, Padmadhara, Karmadhara. Next, he taught the seal and wisdom for accomplishing the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas.
Abiding in all vajra-samādhis, one contemplates the realm of space;
through the vajra-body according to one’s desire, one rises into the air in an instant.
Abiding in all pure samādhis, one cultivates the most supreme.
Having attained the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*) and swiftly accomplished wisdom,
one contemplates Vajrasattva pervading all of space;
once one has firmly brought him to mind, one becomes a Vajradhara.
Visualizing the forms of all Buddhas within the void,
through the meditative absorption (samādhi) of the Buddhas, one shall attain perfect enlightenment.
The mantras for this are as follows:
“Vajra vajra śodhaya śodhaya siddha siddha buddha buddha. As above, this is the accomplishment of the wisdom of all *siddhis*.
"Next, you should cause the disciple to uphold the secret *dharmakṣānti* (endurance) rite. At dawn, they should recite the *praṇidhāna-hṛdaya-mantra*, saying:

Oṃ vajrasattva sarvayantiye kṛtaye samayas tvam niryāpayati tākṣaṇe yāyāni yanimrūya nandane yam. Then, one should address them with these words: 'You must not transgress this *praṇidhāna-hṛdaya-mantra*.
Do not bring upon yourself calamity, misfortune, or an untimely death; lest you fall into hell with this very body.'"

Then one should teach the secret seal-knowledge (*mudrājñāna*); having generated the vajra-entry and entered into meditative equipoise (*samāhita*), even mountains and rocks will be drawn with love by the subtle vajra-palms when they are clapped.
"Next is the Vajra-sphoṭa-mudrā.
Having entered the vajra-ritual, one strikes with the palms in the vajra-bind;
by means of this subtle palm-method, even mountains and rocks are completely penetrated."
By means of the aforementioned rite of entry, extend the vajra-bind;
with a supreme strike, crush [the enemy] as they respond, destroying a hundred clans in an instant.
Through the rite of subtle universal entry, all fingers are held in meditative equipoise (samādhi).
"Binding with the Vajra-bond and releasing it, one is able to seize and overcome all sufferings.
Next, the secret accomplishment shall be explained: having visualized that the Bhaga has entered the body of a woman or a man, cause that body to be completely pervaded."
The heart-mantras for these [deities] are as follows:

VAJRA VAŚYA VAJRA VIŚVA VAJRA HANA VAJRA HARA. Having thus bestowed the heart-mantras, one should instruct them in the four wisdom-mudrās (jñāna-mudrā) of their respective deities, and address the disciples with this ritual procedure:
"Be careful regarding other people; you must not point out these mudrās to anyone who does not yet know them."

Why is this? Because those sentient beings who have not seen the Great Maṇḍala and yet rashly perform these [rites] will find that none are accomplished; they will instead give rise to doubt and confusion, invite calamities, die prematurely, fall into the Avīci Great Hell, and descend into the evil realms.
"Next, the Great Seal Wisdom for the Accomplishment of the Sattvas of all Tathāgatas shall be explained:
'From the mind-wisdom one should generate [the resolve], and one should visualize the Vajra-Sun;
visualizing oneself in the form of a Buddha, one should recite the Vajradhātu.'"
By this, as soon as it is accomplished, one obtains wisdom, longevity, power, and years;
having attained all-pervasive conduct, even the body of a Buddha is not difficult to attain.
This is the seal of the manifest realization of enlightenment (abhisambodhi-mudrā) of all Tathāgatas.
"Next, the Great Seal for the accomplishment of Vajrasattva shall be explained:
'With haughty pride, brandishing the vajra, and maintaining the pride of the vajra,
through the vajras of body, speech, and mind, one becomes Vajrasattva.'"
By means of this seal of universal pervasion, all desires produce bliss;
one attains longevity, power, and superior form, like Vajrasattva.
Following the ritual of the three vajras, practice accordingly as if drawing a painting.
Through the union of signs and mudrās, one accomplishes the Great Sattva.
I shall now explain the various teachings—the means of accomplishment and that which is accomplished—as well as the great activities of the practitioner; I shall now set them forth in sequence.
Every day, first perform the rites according to the proper time, as well as the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*) and so forth;
having completed these as at the beginning, one should thereafter act according to one’s inclination.
Next, the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) shall be explained in detail.
"Having entered the universal vajra, one should form the great mudrā before the body according to the ritual rules;
one should then contemplate the Great Sattva.
Beholding that Jñānasattva, one should visualize him as being within one's own body."
"Summoning, entering, binding, and causing joy bring about accomplishment.
The mantras for these are as follows:
*Vajrasattva Āḥ*. This is the heart-mantra of Vajra-pervasion (*vajrāveśa*).
"Vajrasattva-niḥśeṣaya. This is the heart-mantra for the visualization of the Great Sattva:
"Jah Hūṃ Baṃ Hoḥ. This is the heart-mantra for the Great Sattva’s summoning, entering, binding, and pleasing.
Recite: *samayas tvam*. It enters everywhere behind [the practitioner] as a moon disc;
therein one should visualize the *sattva*, thinking: "I am the *samayas tvam*."
Following that *sattva-mudrā*, practice visualizing oneself as being accomplished through Vajra Speech; one will be able to accomplish all mudrās.
Reciting *jjaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*, the Buddhas enter into one’s body.
One should engage in correct reflection to bring about the accomplishment of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā).
I shall now explain the ritual activities, the unsurpassed Vajra-activity;
through the accomplishment of visualizing the Buddha, one swiftly attains the nature of a Buddha.
Having become the Sattvavajra, one becomes the sovereign of all Buddhas;
by binding the Ratnavajra, one becomes the sovereign of all jewels;
having accomplished the Dharmavajra, one is then able to uphold the Buddha-dharma.
Through the Karma-vajra-mudrā, one becomes a Vajra-karma;
by binding the Sattva-mudrā, one accomplishes Vajrasattva.
One is able to summon the Vajradhara through the Vajra-ākarṣaṇa-saṃyoga.
The Great Seal of Vajra Passion can dye all Buddhas;
it causes all Buddhas to rejoice through the Vajra Well Done;
and it bestows the empowerment of the Buddhas through the ritual of the Jewel Seal.
Swiftly one becomes Vajraprabha through the rite of Vajraprabha;
by holding and practicing the Vajradhvaja, all wishes are fulfilled;
through the rite of Vajrahāsa, one sports and laughs together with all Buddhas.
Having maintained the Vajra Dharma through the ritual of the Vajra Dharma,
one attains the supreme wisdom of all Buddhas through the ritual of the Vajra Sharpness;
by maintaining and practicing the Vajra Wheel, one is then able to turn the Wheel of Dharma.
One achieves the speech of a Buddha through the rite of Vajra Speech;
one swiftly attains Vajra Action by performing Vajra Action;
and by donning the armor of Vajra, one obtains the Vajra Body.
One becomes a Vajra Yakṣa, just like a Vajra Yakṣa;
all mudrās are accomplished by binding the vajra-fist;
through Vajra-lāsyā, one attains great vajra-delight.
By binding the vajra-garland, one receives empowerment from the Buddha;
through union with the vajra-song, one attains the vajra-song;
by performing the vajra-dance, one makes offerings to all Buddhas.
All are made radiant and pleasing by the Vajra Incense;
through union with the Vajra Flower, one causes all classes of beings to be honored;
by means of the Vajra Lamp Seal, through making offerings, one obtains the eye.
One can eliminate all suffering through the ritual of the Vajra Incense;
Through the Vajra Hook, one can perform all supreme activities;
One can cause all to be drawn in through the ritual of the Vajra Lasso.
Through the application of the Vajra-shṛṅkhala, one is capable of all binding;
by means of the rite of Vajrāveśa, one is able to accomplish all paryeṣaṇas.
Next, I shall explain the Vajrasamaya-jñāna-mudrās of all Tathāgatas.
"Join the palms firmly together, with the fingers interlaced;
this is called the Vajra-palms, the supreme Vajra-bind.
All Samaya-mudrās are produced from the Vajra-bind."
I shall now explain the ritual for binding the mudrās, the supreme Vajra-bindings.
With the *sattvavajra* firmly established, the middle fingers are raised like tusks;
the thumb and ring fingers are shaped like jewels, while the middle fingers are bent backward.
Shift the fingers like lotus petals;
with the middle fingers joined together and the index fingers resting upon them, this is called the fifth Buddha.
"I shall now fully explain the supreme mudrā of the samaya of the Tathāgata family."
"By forming the bond, one achieves accomplishment: the two hands are in the shape of a moon;
the middle fingers are like vajras, while the faces of the remaining fingers do not touch.
This is the Vajrasattva mudrā: the supreme fingers are interlaced like hooks at the head."
With the force of a finger-snap, the four Vajrasattvas arise.
These are the various mudrās: for the Jewel-Vajra, join the tips of the index fingers and bend them back;
[the same applies to] the middle, ring, and little fingers.
Extending and rotating them toward the heart, with the ring fingers like banners joined with the little fingers,
and again resting at the place of the smile—
these are called their mudrās; the two thumbs are held upright and aligned.
Bending the index finger like a lotus, it is the Vajra Sword.
Joining the middle fingers and bending their upper joints, it is the Equalizer.
Crossing the ring and little fingers like a wheel, one releases the bind of the thumbs.
Extending [the fingers] from the mouth, with the surfaces of the thumb and little finger joined,
this is the Karma-vajra of the Assembly; then, aligning the index fingers,
one remains composed in mind and extends them, bending the index fingers like fangs.
The little finger is likewise; between the thumb and the little finger, bend the index finger over them.
Aligning it with the thumb at the heart, extend the arms—this is called the *mālā* (garland) mudrā; lift the palms and let them disperse from the mouth.
Performing the dance, join them at the crown; apply the vajra-bind below.
Offering from one's own palms, bring the index fingers together.
Extend them in the manner of anointing, then bend a single index finger.
Binding the two index fingers, with the tips of the thumbs like a lock;
joining them as a vajra-fist, I shall now explain how to achieve accomplishment.
This most supreme vajra-accomplishment consists of abiding in one’s own mudrā at the heart.
The Sattvavajra-samādhi; next, the performance of activities is taught:
the unsurpassed Vajrakarma and the mudrās of the Vajradhātu and others.
Through the assembly of the Tathāgatas, the maṇḍala master [bestows them] upon the disciple.
In an instant, one achieves empowerment by forming the *sattvavajra* mudrā;
thus one becomes a Vajradhara. Merely by forming the *vajrāṅkuśa* mudrā, one can summon all Buddhas, according to the ritual of Kāmadhātuvajra.
Those who are still stained attain perfect awakening through the Vajra Joy;
all rejoice at the sound of "Excellent! through the binding of the Jewel-Vajra;
they receive empowerment from the Buddha through the binding of the Vajra Sun.
Just as the Buddha attains the perfect halo, having held the vajra-banner;
so too, all wishes are fulfilled through the rite of the Vajra-Laughter.
Laughing equally with all Buddhas, one holds the seal of the Dharma-Vajra.
Equal to the Dharma-vajra, he universally wields the vajra-sword;
having attained wisdom as a savior of the world, he practices and holds the vajra-wheel;
thus he is able to turn the wheel of Dharma by means of vajra-speech.
Through the accomplishment of Vajra Speech, one universally holds the Karma-vajra;
equal to Vajra Action, one performs the firm protection of Vajra;
the body is perfected as Vajra, with the supreme seal of the Vajra Fangs.
Able to crush all evil māras, firmly binding the vajra-fist;
Subduing all mudrās in accordance with them, one attains joy through play,
Adornment through garlands, and majestic solemnity through every word.
Through making offerings by means of dance, one attains [graceful] movement; through burning incense, one brings moisture and nourishment to the world;
through the exquisite beauty of flowers, one attains physical majesty; through lamps, the world becomes pure;
and through fragrance, one obtains wondrous scents.
The Vajra-noose brings entry; the Vajra-chain is able to bind;
the Vajra-bell enters everywhere—I now proclaim the Dharma-seal.
Vajrarāja is the Buddha of the South; he is able to establish the firm Vajradhātu.
Next, I shall now fully explain the supreme mudrās of the Dharma-seal according to the original ritual.
By reciting *samayas tvaṃ*, one becomes the sovereign of all mudrās;
by reciting *ānaya sarva*, one is able to summon all Buddhas.
Having recited *ākhusvaka*, one is colored with love for all Buddhas and the like;
having uttered *sādhu sādhu*, they all cause joy by saying "Excellent!";
having recited *sumahātraṃ*, one then obtains the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*) of all Buddhas.
Having uttered "Rūpāṇyudita," one obtains the majestic light of the True Dharma;
by reciting "Athaprāpti," one can fulfill all supreme aspirations;
with the laughter "Ha ha hūṃ hoḥ," one attains the subtle and wondrous smile of the Tathāgata.
Having recited *sarvakāri*, one is able to purify all that is non-Dharma so that it becomes entirely pure;
having maintained the recitation of *nukha-che-na* (pronounced with a retroflex *ṣ*), one is able to sever all karma of painful sensation;
having spoken *buddhabhūmi*, one becomes the sovereign within the maṇḍala.
Having recited *pratīcchāna*, one joins in conversation with all Buddhas;
having recited *svasti-dhvam*, one moves everywhere with mastery;
having spoken *nirvaya-dhvam*, one attains fearlessness in an instant.
Reciting *stambhaya khāda*, one who can devour all enemies;
having recited *sarvasiddhi*, one obtains all sublime siddhis;
*mahārati* brings delight.
Rūpaśubhe likewise;
Śrutarāśaukha obtains happiness;
Sarvapuṣpe obtains offerings.
*Prāharaṇī* obtains fruit; *Sudīptāṅgī* obtains light;
*Sugandhāṅgī* obtains exquisite fragrance.
ĀHĪ JAKṢA performs summoning;
ĀHĪ HŪṂ HŪṂ is able to lead [them] in;
KĪSA PUTA BAṂ is the great attainment.
Kaṇṭha-ak-ak, cause it to tremble!
"I now teach the Dharma-mudrā, which brings about accomplishment and purification.
By visualizing a vajra upon the tongue, one is able to perform all ritual activities."
Next, the *karmamudrā* is explained:
one should form the vajra-fist and, with the mind in meditative equipoise (*samādhi*), divide it into two parts to form the two vajra-mudrās.
Next, the binding is explained: hold them as vajra-fingers.
Placing the right hand upon the left—this mudrā is named "Victorious Awakening.
It bestows the Bodhi of the Buddhas; Akṣobhya has the Earth-Touching mudrā, Ratnasambhava the Wish-Fulfilling mudrā, and Amitāyus the Supreme Samādhi mudrā.
Amoghasiddhi bestows fearlessness; next, I shall now explain in full the sequence of the *karmamudrā*s of Vajrasattva and the others.
Capable of performing vajra-activities, one should [hold the hand] with the left in *māna* (pride) and the right extended and cast forth.
Abiding in the posture of the hook (*aṅkuśa*), one should coordinate it according to the method of archery.
Excellent is abiding in the mind; for the two vajras of consecration, one displays the form of the sun within the mind, with the right elbow resting upon the left fist.
The two palms and the mouth, with the left in the lotus and the right in the opening gesture;
the sword at the heart on the left for slaying, rotating like a wheel of fire.
The two vajra mouths scatter, and the vajra dance rotates.
The two cheeks rest upon the crown; the armor is formed by the little fingers and the teeth.
Joining the two fists together, one should maintain vajra-pride.
Prostrating with a mind of trembling awe, one binds the garland and writes below the mouth.
Performing the revolving vajra dance,
one should offer incense and all other offerings to the Buddhas according to the ritual of the vajra-fist.
For the mudrā of individual offerings, the little fingers are interlaced with one another.
The index fingers are like hooks above; the second fingers are like chains, with the backs of the hands pressed together.
These are the actions of the Vajrakarma and others, which correspond to the Karma-vajra.
One should practice this within the mind.
Next, the Karma-mudrās are explained, consisting of various vajra-activities:
by forming the Wisdom-fist (jñānamuṣṭi), one is able to enter universally into the Buddha-wisdom.
By binding the seal of Akṣobhya, one attains immovability;
by binding the seal of Ratnasambhava, one is able to gather and sustain others;
by binding the seal of the Dharma-wheel, one is then able to turn the wheel of the Dharma.
Through fearlessness, victory, and swiftness, one bestows fearlessness upon sentient beings;
by firmly forming the vajra-garland, there is the bliss of Vajrasattva;
through the vajra-hook, all Buddhas are summoned and assembled in an instant.
The vajra-arrow causes passion, yet it can also serve as the vajra consort;
the vajra-joy of all Buddhas bestows the voice of "Excellent! (Sādhu);
by binding the Great Vajra-Jewel, one receives empowerment from the master.
By universally upholding the Vajra-Sun, one attains the state of the Vajra-Sun;
by erecting the Vajra-Banner and Pennant, one obtains a rain of precious jewels;
by universally upholding the Vajra-Laughter, one swiftly attains the Buddha’s equal laughter.
By universally holding the vajra-flower, one perceives the vajra-dharma;
by firmly binding the vajra-sword, one can sever all suffering;
by universally holding the vajra-wheel, one can turn the wheel of the Dharma.
All the speech of the Buddhas is accomplished through vajra-speech;
even by means of the vajra-dance offering, one causes the Buddhas themselves to be brought into compliance;
and by donning the vajra armor, one attains vajra-like solidity.
Even the Universal Holder of the Vajra Fang can destroy the vajra;
the Vajra Fist can seize it, thereby attaining the accomplishment of the mudrā;
the Vajra Joy brings delight, and the Vajra Garland possesses exquisite color.
The sublime speech of the Vajra song, the Vajra dance that brings all into harmony;
with flowers one seizes all, with lamps the fire blazes intensely,
and with the Vajra incense, the exquisite fragrance.
The vajra hook can summon;
the vajra noose can draw in;
the vajra chain causes binding.
Strike the vajra-bell to signal the commencement.
"I shall now extensively explain the ritual procedure for binding all mudrās.
First, one should perform the 'vajra-binding' strike upon one's own heart while reciting the Heart Mantra as follows:"
"Vajrabandha traṭha. By this, one gains mastery over all mudrā-bindings of the body, speech, and mind-vajras. Then, forming the Vajra-samaya-mudrā of Universal Entry, recite this heart-mantra:
"Aḥ. One thereby becomes the All-pervading Avīśa; like a friend’s empowerment, one should visualize the Great Sattva within the samaya-mudrā and recite this Heart-Vajra-mantra:
"Mahāsamayasatvām hūṃ. Through this mantra, all mudrās are accomplished.
This is the extensive ritual procedure for the accomplishment of all mudrās; it is what I have taught as the complete and extensive ritual rule.
First, one binds one’s own mudrā. Having bound it, one visualizes oneself as the being (sattva) of that mudrā by means of this heart-mantra:
*samayam haṃ*. Once one has visualized oneself as the being of that mudrā, one consecrates [oneself] with this mantra:
“Samayas tvam adhiṣṭhasva sarvam. Only after this should one achieve accomplishment; this is the ritual procedure for accomplishment.
"Next, I shall explain the initial attainment of the accomplishment of desired aims by means of this mantra:
'Aṭhasiddhi. By means of this mantra, one attains the Vajra-accomplishment according to one's wish."
"Next, the accomplishment of Vajrasiddhi is taught by means of this heart-mantra:
*Vajrasiddhi*. Next, the accomplishment of the Vidyādhara is taught by means of this heart-mantra:

*Vajravidyādharā*. By this, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the Vidyādhara according to one's wish; however, if one seeks the most supreme accomplishment, one should seek that accomplishment by means of one’s own seal and mantra."
"I shall now explain how to perform the vajra-ritual within the vajras of one's own body, speech, and mind.
If the empowerment of the mudrā is slow, or if one wishes to release it, then use this heart-mantra to make it firm."
The mantra is:

Oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya | vajrasattva tvenopatishṭha | dṛḍho me bhava | sutoṣyo me bhava | suśrīko me bhava | supoṣyo me bhava | anurakto me bhava | sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha | sarvakarmasu ca me cittaṃ śreyaḥ kuru | hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ | bhagavan sarvatathāgatavajra mā me muñca | vajrībhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ.
SMAI PAVĀVA ANURĀKEDU SMAI PAVĀVA SUBHAISMAI PAVĀVA SARVASIDDHE MAHĀRYACHE SARVAKARMASŪDHE CITTAŚRĪYOGURU HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ BHAGAVAN SARVATATHĀGATAVĀCĀ.
"Vajramatimuncavajri bhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ. By means of this mantra,
even if one has committed the crimes of immediate retribution (ānantarya), slandered all Tathāgatas and the sublime Dharma of the Mahāyāna sūtras,
or performed every kind of evil deed, one shall still attain accomplishment.

“The seal of all Tathāgatas, by virtue of the adamantine and firm body of Vajrasattva, manifests swiftly; according to one’s inclination, one attains all supreme accomplishments... up to the attainment of the supreme siddhi of the Tathāgata.”
The Bhagavān Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas spoke thus:
"I shall now fully explain the ritual procedures for the liberation of all mudrās."
"From each and every [source], one should understand all the mudrās that arise from them by means of this heart-mantra: *vajramuḥ*."

"From one's own mind, arise the Vajra-jewel-mudrā; place it at the site of consecration and perform self-consecration with the supreme finger. Separate the hands to encircle the head and tie the garland."
"Next, bind the armor with this heart-mantra:
*Oṃ vajraratna viśodhaya sarvamudrā-maitrī-karuṇā-varakavaca vaṃ*. Having donned the armor, clap the palms together to inspire joy with this heart-mantra:
'By means of this heart-mantra, one is released from bondage and attains joy.'"
One attains the vajra-body, like Vajrasattva himself.
By reciting the mantra of Vajrasattva even once, one dwells in bliss according to one's heart's desire;
all recitations will swiftly achieve accomplishment, just as Vajrapāṇi has taught.
The Bhagavān Samantabhadra spoke thus:
“Vajrasattva and the other sattvas, perform all accomplishments and activities;
recite this according to one’s intention within it, and all activities will be accomplished.”
Through the mantras, heart-seals, and vidyās, practicing the various *naya*s according to one’s inclination,
whether following what is taught in the scriptures or acting of one’s own accord, one shall attain accomplishment everywhere.
Next, the four kinds of secret offerings are explained; one should perform them with this Vajra Song and Mantra:

*Oṃ vajrasattva saṃgraha vajraratna manohara vajradharma gāyana vajrakarma kāruṇya vasa*. Within the maṇḍala, one should sing with this Vajra Praise, perform the Vajra Dance, and make offerings using the palms of both hands, flowers for offering, and so forth.

Having performed the offerings of vajra incense and so forth at the outer maṇḍala, one should place them in their respective positions and, making offerings to the best of one's ability, address all the Tathāgatas.

Having performed offerings of incense and other items according to one’s inclination, those who have entered the maṇḍala should, according to their capacity, present all flavors of food and drink, comforts, and all necessary requisites to the Great Maṇḍala, ensuring they are fully provided for and enjoyed. One should then bestow upon them the Vajra Prohibitory Precepts (*vajra-saṃvara*) for the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas:
“This is the essential nature of all Buddhas, Residing in the hand of Vajrasattva;
You should now receive and uphold it— The firm prohibitory precept of Vajrasattva.”
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajrasamaya tiṣṭha īśa tvaṃ dhāraya me vajrasattva hī hī hī hī hūṃ. Then, each one was further addressed:
"Do not speak of this to others."
Then, recite the *samayasattva-mantra*; those who have already entered should announce this to all, and the Tathāgata should form the *sattvavajra-mudrā* and release it from below upward.
With this heart-mantra:
*Oṃ kṛtodyoḥ sarvasattvārthasiddhaye tathānugrahārthaṃ caratu buddhaviśramaṇapunarāgamanaṃ te vajrasattva muḥ*. Thus, one performs the release at all maṇḍala-samaya-vijaya-mudrās.
